# scm_dlp_endpoint_policy (Resource)

Manages an Enterprise DLP Endpoint Policy.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An endpoint peripheral-control policy. scope_json and response_json are
# compared semantically, so formatting differences never cause drift.
resource "scm_dlp_endpoint_policy" "block_usb" {
  name        = "Block-Unapproved-USB"
  description = "Block copying to unapproved USB storage"
  type        = "endpoint_peripheral_control"
  severity    = "high"
  enabled     = true

  scope_json = jsonencode({
    user_groups = ["engineering"]
  })

  response_json = jsonencode({
    action = "block"
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the endpoint policy is enabled.
- `name` (String) The name of the endpoint policy.
- `response_json` (String) JSON object representing the policy response/action.
- `scope_json` (String) JSON object representing the policy scope.
- `severity` (String) Severity level: informational, low, medium, high, or critical.
- `type` (String) Policy type: endpoint_peripheral_control, endpoint_data_in_motion, or network.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the endpoint policy.
- `priority` (Number) Priority order of the endpoint policy. Assigned by the backend when omitted.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the endpoint policy.
- `tfid` (String) The Terraform ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing DLP endpoint policy by its ID.
terraform import scm_dlp_endpoint_policy.example <id>
```
